主要内容: On February 29, 2012, the U.S. Department of the Treasury released preliminary data on foreign holdings of U.S. securities as of June 30, 2011. The total foreign holdings were reported at $12,520 billion, with $3,906 billion in U.S. equities, $7,733 billion in long-term debt securities (including $1,141 billion in asset-backed securities and $6,593 billion in non-ABS securities), and $881 billion in short-term debt securities. The data was part of an annual survey conducted jointly by the Treasury, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Final results, including revisions, were expected by April 30, 2012. The survey also included new data on Treasury bond and note holdings as of September and December 2011, improving the accuracy of country attribution for foreign holdings. The new data collection method, which tracks monthly holdings, aims to reduce transactions bias and provide more precise ownership information. The report also breaks down holdings by country, with China (Mainland) holding the largest share at $1.727 trillion, followed by Japan at $1.587 trillion and the United Kingdom at $982 billion.
